plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac-pink goblets rise straight from bare ground, with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows and woodland edges just as autumn begins, and look like crocuses that have lost track of the season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (roughly August to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges across Europe, including the UK, France and Germany
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it isn't a true crocus. It produces colchicine, a toxin that has been used in medicine, and it sends up its leaves in spring, long after the flowers have faded.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: Dense clusters of violet, daisy-like flowers with golden centers light up prairies and roadsides in early autumn. Monarch butterflies stop to feed on them on their long migration south.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through mid-autumn (roughly August to October)
plants.location: Meadows, prairies and roadsides in eastern and central North America
plants.funFact: Its flowers open on sunny days and close in dull or cloudy weather. It is one of the most important late-season nectar sources for migrating monarch butterflies.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Fluffy, fragrant golden pompoms cover the branches in a wave of sunshine yellow. In September, the Australian spring is well underway, and the bush hums with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (roughly August to October in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: It is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
